regulatory_check.note: Checked 2026-11-01. Vermont Quarantine #3 (Noxious Weeds) Class A/B lists no Morus alba, Robinia pseudoacacia, Amorpha fruticosa, Caragana arborescens, Elaeagnus spp. or Salix purpurea. Montana state noxious list (via Flathead County) lists Russian olive (Priority 3, regulated), saltcedar (2B) and common buckthorn (2A); not Caragana, black locust, white mulberry or Siberian elm. Nebraska state list (25 NAC 10-001, checked 2026-11-02) has one woody species, saltcedar (Tamarix ramosissima); the July 2023 county-designated list has none; neither lists Russian olive, Siberian elm, white mulberry, Caragana, black locust or eastern redcedar. The listed_some_jurisdictions flags in this table therefore mark ECOLOGICAL invasiveness concerns (naturalizing, hybridizing with natives), not state regulation; Viridis excludes them as a precautionary policy unless a written override is given.

planting_density_note: plants_per_ha_row = plants per hectare of a 5 m-wide row at species in-row spacing: shrubs ~1.2 m (1,640), apple 1.5-1.8 m (~1,200), mulberry 3 m (670), persimmon/chestnut 6 m (330), large nut and pod trees 9 m (220). Calculated from Savanna Institute, Manitoba, UK CCD and On Pasture spacings.
fruit_composition_note: crop.c_frac and crop.n_kg_t are per tonne of FRESH product: c_frac = dry-matter fraction x 0.45 (fleshy fruit 15-30% DM, chestnut/acorn ~50-55%, nuts in shell and dry pods 85-95%). Approximate composition values; REVIEW.
